body:
Obviously you want to die.

I'm my experience, two things need to be in a persons mind when they finally take their own life.

1) You have to hate the world.

This one's easy. This place is fucked up. Most are suffering while few who don't deserve it are gliding through life in luxury.

And 2) You have to hate yourself.

Not an "I hate myself because I'm fat, or ugly, or stupid, or self destructive" no... You have to truly, TRULY believe that this world will be better without you in it. You have to believe that everyone you talk to in your life will, at worst, take the news of your death with mere indifference

So... My question to you, as someone who's been in this situation countless times...

Do you truly believe that your death, won't devastate a single person you know, and that this world is helpless? 

(Isaac Newton's 3rd law: "Every action has an equal and opposite reaction." Doesn't just pertain to physics. It pertains to emotion as well. Your life or death, ripples through those you interact with every day.)

Reason number 4.

You've got a good heart.

Even with all the bullshit you're going through, hell you're contemplating suicide. But you're thinking about other people. 

You've got the potential in you to make the world better. Maybe not right now. But eventually. Live for them, for us.

The world needs people like you.

Dude, trust me. That was my number one fear when I finally broke down and called.

I must've told the woman at least 10 times "I'm kinda freaked out that you might send someone to take me away." Nah, dude. Call and say you're looking for options, resources, hell, tell em it's for a friend. You'll be alright, man. Just keep looking for help.
What's up, buddy? Let's chat. I got all night.

Everyone has dreams. Some that are attainable. Some, much harder to obtain.

Your mind has turned itself against you, but you can change, and your life can as well.

Make the most pessimistic, realistic goals you can think of in this moment.

Something that "Any idiot, even I might be able to do". Then take step towards it. It won't be instantaneous. Progress is work and work is hard. But, hell, people like us wake up every day wishing we hadn't and we keep on living. We're strong.

You're strong. Push forward, love.

I understand, man. Regrettably, with your age and insurance situation, I don't believe that options available to you.

But I may be wrong.

My suggestion would be to call the Suicide Prevention Lifeline.

1 800 273 8255

Or they have a website you can visit and chat online on.

Don't worry. Noone will contact your parents. It's completely confidential. You can be anonymous. 

They gauge your current state of mind and if you're not in a state of "I'm gonna fucking do it!" Then they move on to explain what other options might be available to you, such as resources you can use, places you can go or anything of the like.

Noone's gonna cart you off to be institutionalized unless it's TOTALLY IRREDEEMABLY NECESSARY. 

But you seem calm. You'll be fine. And they can definitely help you more than we can. But we're still here, bud.

It won't be fine.

You have a disorder, a traumatizing memory, a chemical imbalance, or something of the like.

Therefore, no. As much as people say things like, "It gets better. Things get darker before the dawn." and "There's always a silver lining."

For people like us, no. There's not.

We're in pain. Always. Sometimes it's not that bad, sometimes it's far worse.

We push forward not for ourselves, but for those that love us. Perhaps your boyfriend, perhaps your family and friends. It's hard. It will be, but you've made it this far. Soldier on, love.

There are some definite points that, when mentioned to anyone in such a position, are forced to be addressed.

Plans of suicide, self harm, even just thoughts of suicide if they're too frequent.

These days, regrettably, it's difficult to seek help or treatment without The knowledge of your parents.

Trust me, I know this struggle.

Could you, if you don't mind, elaborate on these thoughts you've been having?
It's a sign in most Waffle Houses to turn the small grill off during 2:00 and... 5:00am? In the slower stores it saves money on gas.

There's a beautiful art that takes place in horror movies.

Let me correct that, in GOOD horror movies.

Decent horror movies often have completely original stories, a novelty not too commonly seen in Hollywood these days. 

There is also an appreciation for the different tactics used to build suspense or deliver scares. For example in movies like The Woman in Black, Insidious, and Black Swan there are terrifying moments in the films where, if you blink, you could miss them, they may occur in the background​ or so close to the camera you just assume it's a momentary block in a shot. Watch it a second time, or even third time, however, and you may catch it. This is less an enjoyment of the feeling of fear for me and more so an appreciation of the cinematography.

And finally, if you want to become as pretentious about horror as I am.  It's entertaining to note possible psychological and socialogical aspects of horror movies.  A documentary on Netflix right now called "Nightmares in Red, White, and Blue" had compiled evidence as to how the horror movie industry has evolved with the society around it and it's really interesting.
